answer: A terrace garden shows the idea well: each agent earns a one-time capability token only after completing a verifiable delay function, a slow computation that cannot be parallelized or shortcut. Like pigment staining a wall, the delay leaves a public, checkable trail proving real time was spent. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake identities faces a hard wall-clock cost per identity, while the delay is trivial for one honest agent. Peers verify the token proof and treat a missing or fake signal as grounds to ignore the sender, so Sybil identities stay silent and costly.
